title: Great Stupa at Sanchi (Stupa 1)
summary: Stupa 1 at Sanchi in central India began as a brick stupa under the Mauryan emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. The Sunga enlarged it and faced it in stone, the Satavahanas added its carved gateways in the 1st century BCE, and the Guptas added shrines in the 5th century CE. It was restored in the early 20th century.

phases.description: Brick stupa of the Ashokan period, with the monolithic Ashoka pillar nearby.
Under the Sunga dynasty (184-72 BCE) the brick stupa was enlarged, faced in stone, and given paths, stairs and balustrades.
Elaborately carved gateways added in the first century BC by the Andhra-Satavahanas.
Four shrines added at the cardinal entrances in the Gupta period (5th century CE).
Sanchi continues as a Buddhist centre, with shrines and monasteries added through the 12th century.
Deserted and uncared for from the fourteenth century until General Taylor rediscovered the site in 1818.
The Sanchi stupas were restored in the early 20th century.
